newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-LIONS SHOULD PLAY HOME TESTS - MCGEECHAN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LIONS SHOULD PLAY HOME TESTS - MCGEECHAN.

text.p: Coach Ian McGeechan wants the British Isles to play home test series as part of northern hemisphere rugby's blueprint for the new professional era.

McGeechan, who will be in charge when the Lions depart in May for a 13-match tour of South Africa, believes there would be huge interest on all sides if major touring sides were given the chance to play the Lions on a regular basis.

"I think we underestimate how big the Lions are in South Africa. They see it as the biggest tour, full stop," McGeechan said on Wednesday after the official unveiling of the Lions' kit, which will include a sponsor's name for the first time.
"I think we should be having test series at home. If South Africa or New Zealand were here, playing against all the home unions followed by a three-test Lions tour, the interest would be incredible."

The Lions concept faced an uncertain future last year when the game turned professional, but McGeechan feels the partnership between the four home unions should be seen as a positive example in the ongoing row between English clubs and the Rugby Football Union (RFU).

"The Lions are going to become very important over the next few years, because they provide both tradition and modernity," he said, looking ahead to a daunting Lions programme which includes three tests on consecutive weekends in Cape Town, Durban and Johannesburg.

"Going to South Africa or New Zealand is the biggest challenge any player will face. This is the first professional tour and playing back-to-back tests on three consecutive Saturdays means we've only got 4-5 weeks to pull everything together.
"But we've just got to accept it and I think there are a lot of talented players who will emerge."
Ray Williams, chairman of the Four Home Unions committee, confirmed the tour was "very definitely on" following discussions with South African Rugby Football Union supremo Louis Luyt last week.
The first Lions tour to the Republic was in 1910. The British Isles only series victory in eight attempts came under Willie John McBride in 1974.
